questions.q: What does this lesson call "the triangle"?
options: Cost, latency, and quality moving together — improving one usually costs on one of the other two
The three main model providers
A diagram of the transformer architecture
The three stages of tokenization
questions.explain: Cost, latency, and quality behave as a three-way trade-off across model tiers — rarely can you improve all three at once.

questions.q: Based on the worked example, what was the daily cost difference between running 1M input + 200K output tokens on Haiku 4.5 versus Fable 5.1?
options: No difference — pricing is identical across tiers
$2.00/day on Haiku vs. $20.00/day on Fable, a 10x spread
$2.00/day on Haiku vs. $4.00/day on Fable
Fable was actually cheaper than Haiku in this example
questions.explain: The worked example calculated $2.00/day on Haiku 4.5 versus $20.00/day on Fable 5.1 for the same token volume — a 10x cost spread purely from tier choice.

questions.q: What does batch processing typically offer, per the lesson?
options: Roughly 50% off standard pricing, in exchange for asynchronous (not instant) turnaround
Guaranteed instant responses at full price
Free usage with no limits
A permanent upgrade to the flagship tier
questions.explain: Batch processing trades immediate response time for a substantial discount — roughly half of standard real-time pricing, per Anthropic's documentation.

questions.q: What does prompt caching reduce the cost of?
options: Output tokens only
Re-reading previously-sent, reused context (like a long system prompt) on subsequent requests
The model's training process
Switching between different providers
questions.explain: Prompt caching lets reused context be re-read at a small fraction of standard input price on later requests, rather than paying full price every time.

questions.q: Why does the lesson emphasize that the exact dollar figures shown will become outdated?
options: Because the figures were never accurate to begin with
Because model pricing changes quickly, so the durable lesson is the pattern (cost/latency scale together, tiers spread widely), not the specific numbers
Because Anthropic refuses to publish pricing
Because pricing never actually changes in this industry
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly separates the exact (soon-to-be-stale) numbers from the durable pattern — cost and latency scaling together, and the value of checking batching/caching — which is the point carried into Lesson 12.
